samples.summary: Read-gating `AttachDocument` leaves a share-link viewer an authorized write path (change pack smuggled in the attach RPC)
samples.evidence: `needWrite = REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method) ? true : attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method)` (line 332-334) forces `needWrite=false` for `AttachDocument`, and `hasAccess` then returns `true` unconditionally for a share visitor whose link matches the document (`return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, line 370). Vector: a viewer holding only a viewer-role share token calls `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (public, no session needed — auth.controller.ts:82-89) to get a Yorkie token, takes the project public key out of any visitor's frontend bundle, builds a bare `yorkie.Client`, does `doc.update(...)` locally BEFORE `client.attach()` so the change rides the attach change pack, and attaches. Yorkie sends `AttachDocument` with verb `rw`; this webhook authorizes it as a read and answers 200; the server applies the pack. Detach + re-attach repeats it, so the bound is one pack per attach, not per client. The document's own read-only mounts (`readOnlyNoteStore`, `readOnlyDocStore`, `_readOnly`) bound only this app's code, not a hand-rolled client. The change itself documents this residual (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:99-106, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md § Risks, docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md), so it is a knowingly accepted trade-off rather than an oversight — but it is an actual write-authorization bypass for the one role the webhook exists to refuse, and it also weakens what `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` buys the public template gallery (a `previewToken` visitor gets the same per-attach write). Closing it needs either a truthful attach verb upstream or rejecting attach-carried packs for non-editors; denying attach outright would break every viewer link, which is why they chose this.

samples.summary: An unscoped `yorkie-service` token is a blanket read/write credential for every document in the deployment, minted by ops scripts and transmitted over the Yorkie transport
samples.evidence: `decideService()` short-circuits on `if (!identity.key) return ALLOW;` (line 289) — before any method, verb, document-key or attribute check — so a token with no `key` claim authorizes every RPC (`PushPull`, `AttachDocument`, and also `ListRevisions`/`GetRevision`/`RestoreRevision`, which the user path deliberately restricts) on every document key in the deployment. Three shipped call sites mint exactly that token: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv()` in scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221 and scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:347 (key omitted), and `sideTokenInjector()` -> `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(secret)` in scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:53. That token is not process-local: the SDK sends it to whatever `YORKIE_RPC_ADDR`/`--target-rpc-addr` names, on every RPC, over a transport that defaults to plaintext `http://` (yorkie.service.ts:49-50), and in the copy script one deployment's credential is deliberately sent to a *different* deployment's Yorkie server. Anyone who can observe that channel or read the Yorkie server's logs gets 10 minutes (or `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN`, which is cast unvalidated from env) of full read/write over all documents — the exact blast radius the per-document `key` claim was introduced to remove for the request path. The stated reason for the exception (one long-lived client walking many documents, token refreshed on the server's schedule) is solvable without an unscoped credential: the injector is a closure and could read a mutable "current document key" the script sets before each attach, or the script could build a client per document as `withDocument` does.

samples.summary: The backend service token is signed with the same `JWT_SECRET` as user session tokens, so one secret now also mints an authorization-check-skipping identity
samples.evidence: `signYorkieServiceToken` signs with the caller-supplied secret, which is `JWT_SECRET` at every production call site (yorkie.service.ts:58, yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv default `process.env.JWT_SECRET`), and `AuthService.verifyYorkieToken` now accepts `typ === 'yorkie-service'` (auth.service.ts:99-105) for a branch that bypasses every Postgres permission check (`decideService`). `JWT_SECRET` already signs session access tokens, refresh tokens (when `JWT_REFRESH_SECRET` is unset, auth.service.ts:59-60) and the client-readable Yorkie user/share tokens. I found no signing oracle that lets a caller control the `typ` claim (`issueYorkieShareToken` puts `typ` first, so a hostile `token` body value cannot override it), so this is hardening rather than an exploit: a distinct secret (or an `aud`/`iss` claim checked only by the webhook's service branch) would keep a compromise of the session-signing key from also yielding an all-documents Yorkie credential.

samples.summary: The script's new "secrets come from the environment, not argv" rule is contradicted by `--database-url` and `--source-api-key`, which still carry credentials on the command line
samples.evidence: The added doc comment (lines 31-33) states the rule — "A secret on the command line is readable by any local process through `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and is echoed into shell history and CI logs" — and the usage text repeats it. Yet `parseArgs` still takes `--database-url` (line 92-95; a Postgres URL embedding the DB password, used at line 156-158), `--mongo-url` (line 96-99; likewise, and passed as an argv element to `execFileSync('mongosh', [...])` at line 201-207 where it is visible in that child's cmdline too) and `--source-api-key` (line 108-111). The same argument that moved the JWT secrets to the environment applies unchanged to these three; leaving them in argv makes the new rule read as covered when only one of four credentials is actually off the command line.

samples.summary: Sheets still has no store-level read-only boundary: only the 5 comment mutators got `assertWritable`, the other ~30 root mutators remain gated by UI conditions only
samples.evidence: The change adds `assertWritable()` to `addThread`/`addReply`/`editComment`/`deleteComment`/`setThreadResolved` with the explicit reasoning that "a UI gate is the wrong last line" (yorkie-store.ts:1298-1311), but every other `doc.update()` mutator on the same class (roughly 30 of them, e.g. lines 271, 326, 367, 406, 497, 529, 624, 699-1187 — cell writes, tab ops, axis ops, images/charts, filter/pivot, `loadQueryResults`) is left ungated, so the sheets store is not the boundary the notes/docs stores are (`readOnlyNoteStore`, `readOnlyDocStore` neuter every non-reader by allowlist). On a viewer-role share mount the protection for those paths is that the affordance is hidden or the engine's `_readOnly` declines — the very arrangement that produced the `CommentPopover` bug this change fixes (`currentUser === null` instead of `readOnly`). Board is the same shape: `YorkieBoardStore.updatePresence` (yorkie-board-store.ts:563-569) has no `readOnly` of its own, and the new guard was added at one of its two call sites (board-view.tsx:596), which is the failure mode the branch's own lessons file names ("the guard goes on the listener you were thinking about"). I audited the currently reachable viewer paths and did not find an ungated one — `datasource-view.tsx:85,125`, `lakehouse-view.tsx:326` (and `LakehouseView` is only mounted from `document-detail.tsx`, not the share route), the pivot panel (`sheet-view.tsx:1682,1691`), and the docs/PDF comment UIs are all `readOnly`-gated — so this is a defence-in-depth/regression-surface finding rather than a live bypass.
searchedFor: grep 'new YorkieStore\(|new YorkieDocStore\(|new YorkieNoteStore\(|new YorkieSlidesStore\(' across the repo
grep 'readOnly' in datasource-view.tsx, lakehouse-view.tsx, notes-toolbar.tsx, shared-document.tsx, packages/frontend/src/app/docs, packages/frontend/src/app/files
read packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts and packages/notes/src/store/store.ts to compare the allowlist boundary
grep 'currentUser === null' for the CommentPopover pattern in docs/ and files/

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as the reviewer describes and I found no compensating guard. `READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument'])` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108) makes `needWrite` false for attach even when the verb is `rw` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:332-334), and the share-visitor branch then returns `true` for any role once the link matches the document (`return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:370) — so a viewer-role link is authorized for AttachDocument. The credential needed is obtainable anonymously: `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` carries no JwtAuthGuard, only throttling (auth.controller.ts:82-90). The only other write gate is `PushPull`, which fires after attach and therefore cannot cover a change pack carried by the attach RPC itself; the repo's own comments concede this (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:99-106) as does the design doc (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:310-314). The client-side read-only mounts are explicitly disclaimed as correctness, not access control, in the controller's own docblock (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:124-130), so they do not guard a hand-rolled client. This is authorization/access control — a write gate weakened for the exact role the webhook exists to refuse — squarely in the Security lane, and being a documented, knowingly accepted trade-off is not a refutation ground. I could not independently verify Yorkie's server-side application of an attach-carried pack (external dependency, not vendored), but the repo asserts that behavior as empirically confirmed, so the uncertainty does not favor refutation.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. yorkie-auth.controller.ts:289 short-circuits `decideService()` with `if (!identity.key) return ALLOW;` as the very first statement — ahead of the CLIENT_METHODS check (294), the empty-attributes fail-closed (299-305), and the per-key equality check (306-314) — so a keyless `yorkie-service` token authorizes PushPull/AttachDocument/ListRevisions/GetRevision on every document key, bypassing the REVISION_READ_METHODS editor-or-member gate at :332-334 that the user path enforces. Keyless tokens are genuinely minted by shipped tooling: signYorkieServiceToken omits `key` when unset (yorkie-service-token.ts:66-68) and yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv never passes a key (:115), used at scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221 and scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:347; copy-yorkie-documents.ts:53 likewise calls yorkieServiceTokenInjector(secret) with no key. The asymmetry is real: yorkie.service.ts:83-87 always scopes the request-path token to one docKey. The credential leaves the process to whatever YORKIE_RPC_ADDR names, defaulting to plaintext http:// (yorkie.service.ts:48-50, scripts' :213/:339), for a lifetime taken unvalidated from env (`as ms.StringValue`, yorkie-service-token.ts:106). No guard makes the branch unreachable — verifyYorkieToken explicitly accepts YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE (auth.service.ts:99-103) and the keyless token is minted deliberately. One supporting detail of the finding is wrong: sideTokenInjector reads each side's own secret with no fallback (copy-yorkie-documents.ts:40-54), so one deployment's credential is NOT sent to another's server; that does not remove the unscoped-credential weakness. Requiring JWT_SECRET to sign limits exploitability to channel observation or Yorkie log access, which is a confidence question, not a severity one, so major stands in-lane as excess authorization scope plus sensitive-credential transmission.

mergedFrom.summary: `READ_GATED_METHODS` makes `AttachDocument` authorize as a read, so a viewer-role share link can write to the document via the attach change pack — the one write the webhook exists to refuse
`READ_GATED_METHODS` downgrades `AttachDocument` to a read check, so a share-link `viewer` can write arbitrary content by carrying a change pack in the attach itself
READ_GATED_METHODS lets a viewer-role share token write: the AttachDocument change pack is applied under a read-only decision

finding.summary: `READ_GATED_METHODS` authorizes `AttachDocument` as a read, so a share-link `viewer` can write via the change pack carried in the attach RPC — repeatably, because `DetachDocument` is unconditionally allowed
finding.evidence:
`READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument'])` (line 108) makes `checkAttribute` compute `needWrite = attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method)` (line 334), i.e. `false` for attach. `hasAccess` then returns `true` for a viewer link whose `documentId` matches (line 370: `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`).

Attacker path: a visitor holding a viewer-role share link POSTs it to the public `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82) to mint a Yorkie token, takes the project public key out of any visitor's bundle, and drives a hand-rolled `@yorkie-js/sdk` client. They build a local `Document`, apply arbitrary local changes, then `attach` — the SDK sends those local changes in the attach ChangePack, and the webhook is asked to authorize the attach only as a read, so it allows. `DetachDocument` is short-circuited to ALLOW before any token check (line 221-223), so the write/detach/re-attach loop is unbounded. That the attach pack is really applied is asserted by this branch's own material: `docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md` explains that `initialRoot`/`initialPresence` seeds ride the attach pack and are therefore refused as a `rw` `PushPull`, which is the entire motivation for the `initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : ...}` fixes in this diff.

Net effect: on the very deployments this PR switches to enforce-by-default, "viewer means read-only" is enforced only against clients that put their changes in `PushPull`. The residual is documented (`docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md` § Risks) and deliberately accepted, but it is still a bypass of the only server-side gate on a viewer's write, and features are being layered on top of it (`assertYorkieAuthEnforced` for the public template gallery).

verdict.reason: Every cited line matched the repository. `READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument'])` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108) makes `needWrite` false for attach at :332-334 even though Yorkie sends verb `rw`, and `hasAccess` then returns `true` for any share-link viewer whose documentId matches (:370). Because AttachDocument in Yorkie carries a ChangePack containing pre-attach local changes — corroborated by this branch's own lessons doc (20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:76-79, "that change rides the attach pack") and conceded verbatim in the design doc's Risks section (yorkie-auth-webhook.md:310-318) — a viewer's writes in that pack are authorized as a read. The loop is unbounded: `DetachDocument` returns ALLOW before any token verification (:66, :221-223). The entry point is reachable by an anonymous attacker: `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` has no JwtAuthGuard and performs no role validation, deferring entirely to this webhook (auth.controller.ts:82-90). I searched for a second gate on the attach-carried pack and found none — the client-side read-only mounts are explicitly disclaimed as non-authorization boundaries by the controller comment (:126-130) and the design doc (:250-257), so `already-guarded` does not apply. This is a share-link role bypass permitting writes, squarely in the authorization/access-control lane, so it is not out-of-scope; a documented and accepted residual is a rationale, not a mitigation, especially as features (assertYorkieAuthEnforced for the public template tier) are being layered on the weakened bound. One minor correction to the reviewer's supporting detail: initialRoot is applied after attach and rides the next PushPull (lessons doc:89-97), not the attach pack; initialPresence is the one that rides attach. This does not change the verdict.
